assumptions: Cases run against a Stripe test-mode account seeded with the synthetic customers described in each case, or against tests/test_outreach_paying_segment.py fixtures offline. No real customer data.
One Stripe account per run. At most eight GET /v1/subscriptions requests, each at most 64000 raw bytes; about 50-60 subscriptions with expanded customers fit in one run.
A customer stayed when they kept paying retention_days after their first paid day. Trial days do not count; younger customers are not judged.
A new subscription within 14 days of the customer's previous one ending is the same customer staying on; unpaid or paused subscriptions with no end date are left out.
cost_drivers: Deterministic Python with no model routes: zero LLM cost and no Tin credits under the bounded-code policy.
Eight Stripe read requests at most. Stripe does not charge for API reads; connected-provider cost is outside Tin's estimate.
Runtime is bounded by the 60-second code window; each request is capped by the gateway's own timeout.
effects: Read-only GET /v1/subscriptions with status=all and the customer expanded, through custom.api.stripe using a restricted key with Read on Subscriptions and Customers.
Writes reports/outreach/PAYING_SEGMENT.md in project state. Emails, names and Stripe IDs are never written; company domains of retained customers are.

No Stripe writes, emails, publication or model calls. It starts no other workflow: the hand-off section lists exact inputs for outreach.email_shortlist, organic.keyword_plan and ads.assessment that the calling agent may start after checking the onboarding plan's hard no's.

cases.description: The ordinary() fixture: 25 work-email customers (20 stay, 12 annual) and 25 personal-email customers (6 stay, 4 cancel in trial, 3 failed payments). Must name work email as the target, personal email as the segment to stop acquiring, annual billing as the offer lever, and write exact start inputs for the shortlist, keyword plan and ads assessment.

contains: Aim at: people who sign up with a work email. 80% of them stayed

Offer lever: customers who pick annual billing kept paying at 100%
"objective": "From the founder's contacts, shortlist people who look like the customers who paid and stayed
